title: Caudal Anesthesia,
tocPath: APPROACH TO PATIENTS WITH EMERGENCY CONDITIONS

blocks.text: Type of epidural block where a LA is injected into the epidural space at the sacral hiatus, the lowest part of the spinal canal. Mainly intended for analgesia in pediatrics.

runs.text: Type of epidural block where a LA is injected into the epidural space at the sacral hiatus, the lowest part of the spinal canal. Mainly intended for analgesia in pediatrics.

blocks.text: B: bupivacaine plain 0.25%, with or without Epinephrine for Caudal block. Dose: 0.5ml/kg- Perineal, 0.75ml/kg T10, 1ml/kg lower thoracic.

runs.text: bupivacaine plain 0.25%, with or without Epinephrine for Caudal block. Dose: 0.5ml/kg- Perineal, 0.75ml/kg T10, 1ml/kg lower thoracic.

blocks.text: D: ropivacaine 0.2% with or without Epinephrine for Caudal block. Target Dose: 0.5ml/kg- Perineal, 0.75ml/kg T10, 1ml/kg lower thoracic.

runs.text: ropivacaine 0.2% with or without Epinephrine for Caudal block. Target Dose: 0.5ml/kg- Perineal, 0.75ml/kg T10, 1ml/kg lower thoracic.

blocks.text: Note: For Caesarean deliveries: Lower doses are required due to physiologic changes of pregnancy: Bupivacaine 0,5% with dextrose, 1.8 mL (9 mg) with or without Fentanyl, 10 mcg (0.2 mL).
